hints.title: Locate the original vertex
hints.body: Complete the square in y to identify the vertex and opening direction of the original curve. Mark the centre of rotation on the same sketch.
hints.recap: A completed square exposes the vertex even when the dependent and independent coordinates are swapped.
hints.pitfall: The centre of rotation is a separate point from the parabola vertex.
hints.pause: Find the vertex and its displacement from the given centre.

recall.reminder: A completed square exposes the vertex even when the dependent and independent coordinates are swapped.

hints.title: Rotate displacements, not absolute coordinates
hints.body: Relative to the centre of rotation, a clockwise quarter-turn sends a displacement (a,b) to (b,−a). Translate back to the usual coordinates after the rotation.
hints.recap: A rotation about a non-origin point can be performed by translating to that point, rotating, then translating back.
hints.pitfall: A clockwise turn and an anticlockwise turn have different signs; test your rule on a point directly right of the centre.
hints.pause: Rotate the vertex and a general point of the curve, then derive and simplify the new equation.

recall.reminder: A rotation about a non-origin point can be performed by translating to that point, rotating, then translating back.

solution:
1. Complete the square. The original equation is x=(y−3)2+2, with vertex (2,3). Relative to P=(−2,3), the vertex has displacement (4,0), which becomes (0,−4) after a clockwise quarter-turn. The new vertex is therefore (−2,−1), and the curve opens downwards.

2. Transform a general point. Write an original point as (a,b) and its image as (X,Y). Relative coordinates give (X+2,Y−3)=(b−3,−(a+2)). Thus b−3=X+2 and a=1−Y.

3. Substitute in the original curve. From a=(b−3)2+2, we get 1−Y=(X+2)2+2, hence Y=−(X+2)2−1=−X2−4X−5.

Answer B. Rotating the whole relation verifies both the new vertex and the width of the parabola.
knowledgePattern: Rotate a sideways parabola about a non-origin centre using relative coordinates
